title: Creamy Seafood Chowder
subtitle: a Maritime-style chowder of cod, shrimp, potatoes and bacon in a creamy, well-seasoned broth
imageAlt: A bowl of creamy seafood chowder with chunks of white fish, pink shrimp, potatoes and corn on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: a big pot: dinner for two, plus 4 bowls for lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw the cod and shrimp in the fridge overnight, or sealed in cold water 30–45 minutes.
Keep it at a gentle simmer once the cream goes in, so it stays silky.

steps.title: Bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium until crisp, 6–7 minutes. Lift out half for the top.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Add the butter, onion and celery and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the flour for 1 minute.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Slowly whisk in the broth, then add the potatoes, dried thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Simmer, partly covered, 12–15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.

steps.title: Seafood
steps.text: Stir in the half-and-half and corn and bring back to a gentle simmer. Add the cod and shrimp and simmer gently 4–5 minutes, without boiling, until the cod flakes at 70°C (158°F) and the shrimp are pink and opaque, 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Discard the bay leaf, taste for salt and ladle into bowls with the reserved bacon on top.

fixIt.fix: Mash a few potato cubes against the pot and simmer 2 minutes.
It boiled after the cream went in. Keep it just under a simmer.
Stir gently once the fish is in; big chunks hold together better.

saleTip: Frozen cod and shrimp go on sale together at No Frills before Lent and in summer; stock up then.
swap: Haddock or pollock for cod; a 142 g can of baby clams with juice for some of the shrimp.
leftovers: Reheat gently; don't boil or the seafood toughens.
doneness: Cod at 70°C (158°F), shrimp at 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, fish and shellfish). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested Maritime seafood chowder methods (Canadian Living, Taste of Nova Scotia): a bacon, onion and potato base thickened with flour, finished with cream and gently poached cod and shrimp.
prepAhead: Make the potato base up to 2 days ahead; bring to a simmer and add the cream and seafood just before serving.
reheat: Gently over medium-low, stirring, without boiling, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Cod and potato chowder; no shrimp, corn or bacon.

stepNotes.0: Basic: skip the bacon; start with the butter.
stepNotes.3: Basic: cod only, no corn or shrimp.

fancy.note: Scallops added with the seafood, and oyster crackers on top.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: add the scallops with the shrimp; they're done when opaque, 74°C (165°F).

plating: Bacon and crackers scattered on top.
Warm crusty bread on the side.

why.1-3: Half-and-half gives a creamy chowder without being heavy.
why.0-4: A little flour keeps the cream from separating and thickens the broth.
why.0-0: Bacon gives the smoky depth of a Maritime chowder.

funFact: Chowder may come from the French 'chaudière', the big cauldron Breton fishermen cooked their catch in.

keeps.note: potatoes and cream go grainy when frozen

drink: An unoaked Chardonnay, or apple cider.
